tests.name: app-bruteforce-attack
tests.description: 5 failed logins from one IP within 2 minutes, non-allow-listed accounts, must trigger the brute-force correlation rule.

tests.name: app-bruteforce-benign-service-account
tests.description: 5+ failed logins from an allow-listed automation account must stay suppressed - by whichever allow-list rule (100901 individually, 100903 on the correlation) ends up being analysisd's most-specific match; both are level 0, so the observable security outcome (no alert) is identical either way. Which exact rule ID 'wins' among same-level siblings on the 5th line is an undocumented engine implementation detail, not a behavior worth asserting on - see docs/detections/100900-app-bruteforce.md.

tests.name: lsass-mimikatz-attack
tests.description: Non-allow-listed process reading LSASS with a Mimikatz-consistent access mask must hit the high-confidence rule (and only it - the more specific 100912 overrides its silent parent 100910).

tests.name: lsass-defender-benign
tests.description: Windows Defender's legitimate LSASS access must resolve to the allow-list suppression rule (100915), never to the dumping rule (100912).

tests.name: process-injection-shellcode
tests.description: CreateRemoteThread with no backing module must trigger the shellcode-injection rule (and only it - target process is deliberately outside the sensitive-process list in 100922 to avoid an unrelated sibling-rule ambiguity).

tests.name: powershell-encoded-attack
tests.description: PowerShell ScriptBlock with -enc/-nop/-w hidden/download-cradle indicators must be flagged suspicious (100931 overrides its silent parent 100930).

tests.name: powershell-benign-admin-script
tests.description: Ordinary signed admin scriptblock logging must not trip the suspicious-content rule.

tests.name: credential-access-full-chain
tests.description: injection -> LSASS dump -> suspicious PowerShell within 5-minute windows must escalate all the way to the level-15 incident rule (one rule id per stage - each is the most specific match for its own event).

tests.name: credential-access-chain-fires-without-time-bound
tests.description: Regression test for a documented engine limitation, not a boundary check: this repo originally expected a 10-minute gap between injection and LSASS dump to NOT escalate to rule 100941 (a real 5-minute timeframe). It does escalate anyway - Wazuh's if_matched_sid only supports a true time-bounded window when paired with frequency>=2 (volumetric correlation), which doesn't fit a single-occurrence chain like this one. See the header comment in rules/100940-credential-access-chain.xml for the two rounds of real CI failure that established this. This test asserts the actual, current behavior (fires regardless of gap) so a future change that accidentally narrows it doesn't go unnoticed.
